goal: Consolidate scattered block-template creation, submission, and tip-waiting logic into one BlockTemplateManager class.
Removes NodeContext::mining and duplicate copies of template data, and lets RPC and tests bypass the IPC mining interface entirely.
Framed by the author as a pure refactor that preserves existing behavior.
reviewability: Five reviewers have re-ACKed the latest rebase and no material blocking question is open; a reviewer's suggestion to drop the fuzz-test commit is non-blocking follow-up, not a review blocker.
agreement: Strong support from multiple maintainers/contributors with concrete reasons across many review rounds (Sjors, pablomartin4btc, w0xlt, enirox001).
Nonblocking criticism that the new fuzz harness doesn't effectively exercise BlockTemplateManager and should be reworked or split out, not yet addressed (marcofleon).

result.summary: This PR introduces node::BlockTemplateManager, a new class that owns block template creation, submission, and mining tip-wait helpers, replacing scattered logic previously spread across NodeContext, miner.cpp, the interfaces::Mining implementation, and RPC. RPC methods (getblocktemplate, generateblock, waitfor*) and tests now call BlockTemplateManager directly instead of going through the IPC-facing Mining interface, removing NodeContext::mining/EnsureMining and eliminating several redundant CBlock/vector copies along the way. A new fuzz target for BlockTemplateManager::CreateNewTemplate() is added. The author describes it as intended to be a pure refactor that preserves existing behavior.
result.problem: Mining-related state and helper functions (template creation, submission, tip-waiting) were duplicated and dispersed across NodeContext, miner.cpp, the mining interface, and RPC, making it hard to reason about and extend. This scattering is a concrete blocker for planned follow-up work (per-call memory tracking in #33922, fee-inflow tracking in #35581) that needs a single owner for template state.

open_concerns: marcofleon (2026-09-16) argues the new fuzz harness mostly tests BlockAssembler-via-fuzzed-mempool behavior rather than BlockTemplateManager itself, and that WaitTipChanged/WaitAndCreateNewBlock/CooldownIfHeadersAhead/SubmitBlock paths are barely exercised with zero timeouts; he suggests dropping the last fuzz commit and doing it as a separate, reworked PR, explicitly calling this non-blocking for the refactor.

enirox001 raised a design note that SubmitBlockStateCatcher logic is now duplicated in three places (BlockTemplateManager, rpc/mining.cpp, util/mining.cpp) and could be unified in mining_types.h, explicitly deferred to a follow-up PR.
resolved_concerns: Sjors' early requests for smaller commits, naming (BlockCreateArgs, m_block_create_args), IWYU enforcement for new files, and avoiding redundant copies were implemented across several force-pushes.

pablomartin4btc's finding that CreateBlockTemplateManager() was called in ChainTestingSetup's constructor before chainstate activation (would crash on CreateNewBlock) was fixed by moving the call after LoadVerifyActivateChainstate() in each path.
w0xlt caught that the rebase after #34672 had reverted some of that PR's SubmitBlock changes; fixed.
w0xlt caught a missing block_template_manager reset/recreate in wallet/test/fuzz/fees.cpp; fixed.

result.card: This PR introduces node::BlockTemplateManager, consolidating block-template creation, submission, and tip-wait logic that was previously scattered across NodeContext, miner.cpp, the interfaces::Mining implementation, and RPC, and routes RPC methods and tests through it directly instead of the IPC mining interface. The author frames it as a pure, behavior-preserving refactor; its strongest evidence of importance is that it is an explicit prerequisite for two other open mining PRs (#33922 memory-load tracking, #35581 fee-inflow tracking) that share commits with it and build on this foundation, plus incidental removal of several redundant template-data copies in getblocktemplate. Review state is strong: five distinct reviewers (Sjors, pablomartin4btc, w0xlt, enirox001, and marcofleon) engaged across many rounds, with re-ACKs on the latest rebase (e8b283c35a) from four of them. The one open thread is marcofleon's non-blocking critique that the newly added fuzz harness doesn't effectively test BlockTemplateManager and should be split into a separate, reworked PR. No dependency blocks this PR from merging; it instead blocks other stacked mining work.
